newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda okays use of Entebbe for Zaire relief.
newsitem.headline: Uganda okays use of Entebbe for Zaire relief.

text.p: Uganda's foreign ministry said on Wednesday the government had agreed to the use of Entebbe airport as a base for international relief operations in the eastern Zaire crisis.

"We have previously said that they (the international community) can use Entebbe as a base for the relief efforts for the refugees in eastern Zaire and that has not changed," Ugandan foreign ministry spokesman Louis Balinda told Reuters.
Canada, impatient with the indecision on the eastern Zaire refugee crisis, on Tuesday proposed that a military headquarters for relief operations be set up in Uganda.
Uganda's Balinda said a United States relief advance team had already set up base at Entebbe "and we see no problem with the Canadians joining their brothers there".
Uganda borders Zaire, but does not have easy road links with the area the refugees are in.

The U.N. Security Council mandated a Canadian-led military force for eastern Zaire on November 15, but the subsequent return of about 600,000 refugees into Rwanda and confusion over how many still remain has caused lengthy reassessment.
"Our view is that there needs to be some decisions soon on a course of action," Canadia Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Tuesday.

"So we'll be proposing to our partners -- and we hope we can get some closure in the next 24 hours -- that we go ahead with the establishment of a military headquarters operation in Entebbe to help coordinate matters and prepare for future actions, including reconnaissance flights into Zaire."
